node_definition.done_when: The the-suite-is-green-at-head followup f-sgh-shared-basetemp-destroys-a-peer holds. s22's measurement is at ~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s22-coord/reflex-tests-environment/report.md. A pytest session given an explicit --basetemp takes a lock beside it (a file next to the basetemp directory, not inside it, since pytest removes and recreates the directory) and holds it for the whole session. A second session starting on the same basetemp while a live pid holds the lock is refused before pytest removes anything, and the refusal names the holding pid and the basetemp. A stale lock whose pid is dead is taken over. A sequential second session on the same basetemp starts normally. tests/conftest.py carries this as a session-scoped hook. tests/test_a_shared_basetemp_is_refused.py drives three cases, each with two child pytest processes in a temporary directory outside any repository. 1: the second session is refused naming the first's pid, and the first session's fixture files are intact afterwards. 2: a session started after the first has exited runs normally on the same basetemp. 3: a lock left by a dead pid is taken over. The declared negative control is executed and logged under pytest: remove the lock in a scratch tree, and case 1's second session deletes the first's fixture directory, so the case fails. tests/conftest.py's existing session checks (the scheduler guard and the producer reaper) keep their behaviour. The test files under tests/ are run at base and at head with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under $TMPDIR, and they add no failing id. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=. Only tests/conftest.py and the new test file change.
